title: Industry and occupational employment projections overview and highlights, 2024-34 (Monthly Labor Review)
date_evidence: The article 'Industry and occupational employment projections overview and highlights, 2024-34' was published in the Monthly Labor Review on January 8, 2026.
key_claim: Automation, including AI, is expected to contribute to declining employment in office and administrative-support occupations over 2024-34 - the coordination, scheduling and information-relay work that has historically defined much of the middle-management and supervisory layer.
notes: Tier 1 government statistics. Anchors the structural-automation backdrop to coordination work; used directionally for the mechanism, not for a manager-specific count.

title: State of the Global Workplace 2026 / Span of Control: What's the Optimal Team Size for Managers?
date_evidence: The Gallup State of the Global Workplace: 2026 Report was published in April 2026 ... the average number of people reporting to managers has increased from 10.9 in 2024 to 12.1 in 2025.
key_claim: The average number of direct reports per US manager rose from 10.9 in 2024 to 12.1 in 2025, a nearly 50% increase since Gallup began measuring in 2013; manager engagement fell from 31% in 2022 to 22% in 2025 (a five-point drop in 2024-25 alone); manager engagement declines as span of control widens, though talent and training can partly offset it.
notes: Tier 2 quality data provider. Primary quantification anchor for span widening and the manager-overload stress point.

title: The State of Organizations 2026: Three tectonic forces that are reshaping organizations
date_evidence: The latest McKinsey's State of Organizations 2026 report ... published in February 19, 2026 ... familiar productivity plays (restructuring, delayering, downsizing, cost cuts) are hitting diminishing returns.
key_claim: Familiar productivity plays - restructuring, delayering, downsizing, cost cuts - are hitting diminishing returns; the larger opportunity is redesigning how work moves across the enterprise (workflows, handoffs, decision rights) rather than further cutting layers.
notes: Tier 2 consultancy. Used as the sourced counter-argument: delayering as an end in itself yields diminishing returns.

title: 88% of leaders are confident their reorganization will deliver - only 36% of employees agree
date_evidence: BOSTON-January 29, 2026-Most organizational redesigns are intended to change how people work ... Ninety percent of middle managers surveyed reported considerable changes to their work ... only 22% of employees surveyed said they received sufficient support.
key_claim: In a survey of nearly 1,000 executives and employees who had undergone a reorganization, 88% of leaders believed the new structure would meet its goals versus only 36% of employees; 90% of middle managers reported considerable changes to their work, yet only 22% of employees received sufficient training, coaching or tools; reorganizations are accelerating to capture generative-AI benefit.
notes: Structural anchor (29 Jan 2026, ~4 months). Canonical recent institutional evidence that the reorganization wave centres on the middle-manager layer and is under-supported.

title: The megamanager era: AI is doubling bosses' workloads - and the costs are just beginning to show
date_evidence: fortune.com/2026/04/07/megamanager-era-how-many-direct-reports-ai-middle-management ... average span of control is now 14 and still rising, with some managers carrying 90 direct reports; LinkedIn job postings with 'manager' in the title declined 12% year-over-year in early 2026 while 'lead' and 'principal' postings grew 18%.
key_claim: Average span of control has risen toward 14 with some managers carrying up to 90 reports; Meta's applied-AI engineering division deployed a 50-to-1 employee-to-manager ratio; LinkedIn postings with 'manager' in the title fell 12% year-on-year in early 2026 while 'lead' and 'principal' postings rose 18%, evidence of a structural bifurcation between a thin manager spine and an expanding expert track.
notes: Tier 3 journalism. Source for threshold-crossing spans (50:1, 90) and the manager-title vs lead/principal divergence.

title: The middle manager cuts saving you millions today will cost you everything in 2028
date_evidence: fortune.com/2026/04/12/middle-manager-cuts-leadership-pipeline-crisis-2028-2 ... the middle manager cuts saving you millions today will cost you everything in 2028 (leadership-pipeline crisis).
key_claim: Removing the middle-management layer hollows out the leadership pipeline: coaching, mentorship and on-the-job development - the soft infrastructure that builds future senior leaders - are the first casualties of span-of-control inflation, creating a succession deficit that lands around 2028.
notes: Tier 3 journalism. Source for the second-order pipeline/succession breakage that is the non-obvious core of the signal.

title: Managers Are Being Stretched Thin As Average Team Size Jumps To 12 Workers
date_evidence: allwork.space/2026/01/managers-are-being-stretched-thin-as-average-team-size-jumps-to-12-workers ... average team size jumps to 12 workers.
key_claim: Independent trade coverage of the Gallup span-of-control finding, corroborating that average team size has jumped to roughly 12 and that managers are being stretched across wider spans.
notes: Tier 3 trade press. Independent corroboration of the Gallup span figure.
